summary: Raffaele Pettazzoni (1883–1959) worked in religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Bologna and Sapienza University of Rome, later serving as incaricato at Bologna (1914–1922) and full professor of history of religions at Rome (1923–1958).

Raffaele Torella (born 1950) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied under Raniero Gnoli (~1970–1976) and served as a faculty member at Sapienza University of Rome from approximately 1980 to 2020.
Raffaello Orlando specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Princeton University in 1981, studying under Denis Twitchett.

Raghu Ananthanarayanan is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied engineering at IIT Madras and studied under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya and T. K. V. Desikachar, later teaching at Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram and IIM Ahmedabad (attested 2010).

Raghu Vira (1902–1963) worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Punjab and Leiden (under Willem Caland and Ralph Lilley Turner), served at Sanatan Dharma College (~1929–1946), and directed the International Academy of Indian Culture.

Raghunath Damodar Karmarkar (1893–1964) worked in Indology and philosophy. He served as principal of Sir Parashurambhau College (attested 1970) and as director of the Post-Graduate and Research Department and professor at Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.
Raghunath Giri was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied under Vamacharana Bhattacharya and served as a department head at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

Rahul Parson is an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley (2004–2012). He held assistant professor posts at the University of Colorado Boulder (2016–2020) and UC Berkeley (2021).

Rahul Peter Das (born 1954) specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Klaus Ludwig Janert and Albrecht Wezler, completing his degrees at Hamburg. He taught at Hamburg, Bonn, Groningen, and Marburg, and held a professorship at Halle-Wittenberg (1994–2020).

Rahul Sankrityayan (1893–1963) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He held a Sanskrit teaching position at Vidyalankara Pirivena (1927) and taught Sanskrit and held a professorship at Saint Petersburg State University (1937, 1945–1947).

Raimo Anttila (1935–2023) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied under Warren Crawford Cowgill at Yale University (~1961–1966) and held academic posts at UCLA (1965) and the University of Helsinki (1971–1976).

Raimon Panikkar (1918–2010) was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Barcelona, Bonn, Madrid (under Juan Zaragüeta), and the Lateran. He held teaching posts at Madrid (1946–1953), Harvard (1966–1971), and UC Santa Barbara (1971–1978).

Raimond Gaita (born 1946) is a philosopher educated at Melbourne and Leeds. He served as Foundation Professor of Philosophy at Australian Catholic University (1993–2011) and Professor of Moral Philosophy at King's College London (1977–2011).

Raj Ballav Panda is an Indology scholar who earned degrees from Rajendra University, Centurion University, and Banaras Hindu University (PhD 2022). He held posts at Rajendra University in 2018 and Klorofeel School in 2022.
Raja Pathak is an Indologist who completed a PhD at Banaras Hindu University (2014–2020) and holds a post at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.

Raja Ram Shastri (1904–1991) was an Indology scholar and Lok Sabha member (~1971–1977). He also served as chairman of the managing committee at Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University (attested 1976).

Rajan Gurukkal (born 1948) works in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Calicut and JNU, he directed the School of Social Sciences at Mahatma Gandhi University (1988) and held visiting roles at Berlin, EHESS, and IISc.

Rajan Khatiwoda (born 1984) is an Indologist and historian. After earning a PhD from Heidelberg University (2013–2017), he held posts at Heidelberg University and the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (2017–2026).
Rajaram Hegde is a scholar of history, archaeology, and religious studies. In 2010, he was attested as director at Kuvempu University and the Centre for the Study of Local Cultures.

Rajat Pal is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He completed an MA at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya (2018–2020) and undertook PhD studies at the Indian Institute of Technology Madras (2022–2026).
